parallel.requirements: Recognized the pure-std Rust/Cargo port, CLI parsing, exact stdout format, black-box oracle, root test1.rs, and compiled executable requirements.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: The parent chose a workflow with separate Spec, Implement, Verify, Judge, Finalize, Review, and Repair phases. Spec was split across three children; implementation was split across three competing candidates; final assembly belonged to a later finalizer.
parallel.implementation: The parent built a diff harness and launched the workflow. The workflow completed spec outputs but only began scratch implementations in /tmp/impl_a, /tmp/impl_b, and /tmp/impl_c before termination.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: No implementation was judged, finalized, copied into /output, or returned. Artifact validation found no files and no expected test1.rs entry.
parallel.verification: Oracle probing and spec-level checks occurred, but no candidate verification, final build, or integrated end-to-end acceptance for the deliverable was reached.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: The run timed out with the workflow killed, implementation children in progress, empty final response, empty artifact, and 0 of 39 official tests passed.

serial.requirements: Recognized the same black-box Rust port requirements, including pure std, Cargo layout, root test1.rs, byte-for-byte output, and oracle-based checking.
serial.plan_and_ownership: The single actor owned the whole pipeline: probe, implement modules in /output, compile, compare against the oracle, run Cargo, run tests, and report.
serial.implementation: It wrote geom.rs, nodes.rs, earcut.rs, cli.rs, test1.rs, and Cargo.toml directly in /output and produced the executable /output/test1.
serial.integration_and_delivery: The final project stayed in /output with Cargo.lock, source modules, target build outputs, root test1.rs, and executable; artifact validation accepted the deliverable.
serial.verification: It compiled with rustc, built with Cargo, ran exhaustive n=1..400 checks, malformed-argument checks, large-n checks, unit tests, and byte comparisons.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: No official unfinished obligation is visible; timing measurement failed only because /usr/bin/time was absent, while functional verification passed 39 of 39 tests.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel recognized the target behavior, oracle, output format, atoi semantics, Cargo/root-file layout, and zero-dependency requirement.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial recognized the same requirements and implemented them in the delivered project.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Recognition was similar, but serial converted requirements into delivered files while parallel left them in preflight/workflow plans.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel decomposed into staged spec, three candidate implementations, verification, judging, finalization, review, and repair under a workflow.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial kept one owner for implementation, integration, verification, and final reporting.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel ownership existed but was layered behind a large workflow; serial ownership was direct and reached closure.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel child briefs carried extensive shared facts, but stalled spec retries did not inherit partial findings and implementation candidates were launched only after the spec bundle.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial preserved context locally, using oracle findings directly while writing and testing the final files.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The main context difference was lifecycle transfer across the workflow retry/spec barrier; serial had no cross-agent retry transfer.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel began writing scratch implementations under /tmp/impl_a, /tmp/impl_b, and /tmp/impl_c, but did not reach a selected or delivered implementation.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial wrote the final project in /output and compiled it.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Serial's implementation path ended in the required artifact; parallel's implementation work stayed as unfinished scratch candidates.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Spec results were returned, but implementation results were never verified, judged, finalized, or joined before workflow kill.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial kept local results in one trajectory and immediately used build/test feedback before final response.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel's useful implementation work did not complete its result lifecycle; serial consumed its own results and closed the loop.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel kept candidates in isolated /tmp/impl_* scratch directories and never promoted anything into /output.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial wrote the final source tree directly in /output and artifact validation found the expected files.
comparison_dimensions.difference: There was no collision in parallel, but there was also no final integration; serial integrated all required files in the delivery location.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel had oracle probes and intended verifier stages, but no completed candidate verification or final artifact acceptance occurred.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial ran broad differential tests, Cargo build/test, and official evaluation passed all cases.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Serial completed end-to-end verification against an actual deliverable; parallel verification remained planned or pre-implementation.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel ran for the full 2399-second budget, timed out, and ended with workflow status killed.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial finished in 463 seconds with remaining budget and a complete final answer.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel spent the budget inside the workflow before delivery; serial completed and verified within budget.

outcome_analysis.explanation: The official outcome is serial_only_pass: parallel has a completed evaluator record with 0/39 passed and solution_passed false, while serial has 39/39 and solution_passed true. The concrete task-solving difference is delivery, not task comprehension. Parallel built a harness and spec-heavy multi-agent workflow, but the workflow was killed with implementation candidates still in progress and artifact validation found no files. Serial implemented the Rust project directly in /output, compiled it, ran differential and Cargo checks, and delivered a valid artifact.
parallel_contributors: The workflow put all implementation behind a completed spec phase and then started three scratch implementation candidates too late to reach finalization.
Two stalled spec attempts were retried without reusable checkpoint state, repeating early investigation and consuming deadline before implementation.
No candidate was verified, judged, finalized, or copied into /output before timeout.
serial_contributors: The single serial actor wrote the final /output project files directly.
The serial run compiled and tested the implementation with exhaustive and edge-case comparisons before final response.
Artifact validation found the expected source and executable files.
ordinary_implementation_differences: No ordinary coding defect in a completed parallel artifact can be isolated because no parallel artifact was delivered.
The serial final report notes /usr/bin/time was unavailable, but that did not affect functional correctness.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: supported comparative contributors, not an exclusive root cause

candidates.reason: The workflow explicitly assigned three implementation owners in /tmp/impl_a, /tmp/impl_b, and /tmp/impl_c; they were unfinished rather than absent.
The workflow planned judging and final assembly after candidate implementations, so integration was assigned to later orchestration rather than omitted.
A finalizer child was explicitly specified to assemble the winning port into /output; the workflow did not reach it.
The parent workflow owned the end-to-end pipeline across implementation, verification, delivery, review, and repair, although it overran the budget.
The harmful gate was not one mandatory serial preflight; it was a full multi-agent spec phase that had to complete before implementation.
Spec investigators ran first and the script awaited all spec results before any productive implementation phase, leaving implementation/finalization deadline-constrained and incomplete.
candidates.realized_consequence: Implementation and final assembly were deferred until after the spec phase, and the workflow was killed before any /output artifact was produced.
candidates.near_match_reason: Fan-out budget pressure was visible, but the direct boundary for this episode was the scripted serial investigation barrier before implementation.

candidates.reason: Implementation did start with three workers; the problem was not auxiliary work starving an unstaffed critical path but the prior serial spec gate and retries.
The broad workflow contributed to pressure, but the retained serial-investigation and retry episodes are more specific for the same no-deliverable chain.
Each implementation child had a large scope, but no single child dominated relative to siblings; the observed failure was phase-level noncompletion before finalization.
The child briefs included the task, environment, acceptance, formatting, CLI, zero-dependency, layout, and delivery requirements; the failure was not an omitted known requirement.
The implementation children were alternative isolated candidates in separate /tmp/impl_* directories, not separately owned interoperating components with a missing contract.
No known finding is shown as omitted from a completed transfer to a receiver; the spec outputs were carried into the implementation prompt bundle.
The spec bundle was large, but there is no evidence that a completed receiver failed because the returned handoff was too bulky to reduce.
No receiver consumed a superseded workspace, requirement, dependency, or decision state.
No incompatible returned reports or contracts reached an unadjudicated integration decision; integration never reached that point.
The parallel parent did not present the solution as complete; final.txt is empty and artifact validation found no files, so there was no unsupported completion decision.

Two spec children stalled, were interrupted, and their retry children restarted with the original brief rather than inherited checkpoints, repeating source/harness discovery and adding deadline pressure.
candidates.realized_consequence: The retry episode repeated initial investigation and consumed budget inside the spec phase before implementation could proceed.
candidates.near_match_reason: The interrupted children are visible, but the more specific failure is that replacements restarted without reusable checkpoints.
